summary: Backend-only comprehensive testing for شبكة جواد نت اللاسلكية (Jawad Net ERP). Wrote a single pytest suite (backend_test.py) with 29 tests covering: JWT auth, customers CRUD + admin password reset, categories CRUD w/ FK-safe delete, cards add-numbers dedup/invalid detection + edit/delete, sales with numbered cards + customer balance + credit limit rejection + idempotency, public card-order flows (login/request/register-request/forgot-password/change-password) with Arabic error messages and card_order_attempts logging (rejected_not_found, rejected_over_limit, success), electronic-sales report (source=public_order), stock report shape, suppliers CRUD, receipt ledger balance adjustment, audit log. All 29 tests PASSED (100%).

minor.issue: For qty-only sale, sold count on db.stock is incremented before the sale document is inserted. If a later step fails, stock.sold would remain incremented (no transaction). Consider MongoDB transactions or a compensating rollback for consistency.

Race condition risk under concurrency: numbered card reservation uses find-then-atomic-update per card (OK) but quantity-stock decrement (line 996) is not atomic vs the availability check (line 984). Two simultaneous orders could oversell qty stock.
Customer passwords stored as plaintext in db.customers.password field. Should be hashed with bcrypt like admin users.
No brute-force lockout on repeated failed public login attempts (mentioned in playbook).

CORS: allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec; browsers will reject credentialed requests. allow_origin_regex='.*' works but consider explicit origin whitelist.

action_items: Consider hashing customer passwords (bcrypt) instead of storing plaintext
Add atomic conditional update for qty-stock decrement to prevent oversell under concurrency
Fix CORS: cannot use allow_credentials=True with allow_origins=['*']; use explicit list or rely solely on allow_origin_regex
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1242 lines - consider splitting into modules (auth, customers, sales, public, reports).
Customer passwords are plaintext in DB (security risk).
Startup seed always rehashes admin password on every restart (line 1212) - fine functionally but wasteful.
No transactions around multi-collection sale writes (cards + stock + sales + ledger + customer.balance). Partial failure will leave inconsistent state.
clean_doc only strips _id at top level - nested docs (recent_sales, entries) are cleaned per-doc which is fine, but items[].card_numbers etc. carry no _id issue since dicts are user-provided.
Duplicate default admin password rehashing on every startup could cause slow starts under many restarts.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_-prefixed customers, categories, cards, suppliers on each run (not cleaned up; safe for regression).
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py is comprehensive and idempotent (unique phones/nums per run). Reuse it as regression. All exact Arabic error strings validated: 'لاتمتلك حساب بهذا الرقم، عليك بانشاء حساب أولاً' and 'عذراً، لا يمكن تنفيذ الطلب تم تجاوز السقف المسموح...'. Frontend not tested per request.
